items.originalSummary:
Release: llm-coding-agent 0.1a0

Another Fable 5 experiment. Now that my LLM library has evolved into more of an agent framework it's time to see what a simple coding agent would look like built on it.

I started a new Python library using my python-lib-template-repository GitHub template repository, then ran these two prompts (here's the Claude Code for web transcript):

Write a spec.md for this project - it will depend on the latest “llm” alpha from PyPI and implement a Claude code style coding agent complete with tools for reading and editing files and executing commands

Then:

Commit the spec, then build it using red/green TDD in a series of sensible commits (each with passing tests and updated docs) - occasionally manually test it using the OpenAI API key in your environment

Here's the spec, the resulting README file, and the sequence of commits.

I've shipped a slop-alpha to PyPI, so you can run the new agent like this:

uvx --prerelease=allow --with llm-coding-agent llm code

It's pretty good for a first attempt! Here's the (Fable-authored) README, which lists recipes like llm code --yolo and llm code --allow "pytest*" --allow "git diff*".

It also presents a Python API based around a CodingAgent(model="gpt-5.5", root="/path", approve=True).run("Fix the failing test in tests/test_parser.py") class which I didn't ask for but I'm delighted to see implemented.

Here's the suite of tools it implemented, listed using uvx ... llm tools:

CodingTools_edit_file(path: str, old_string: str, new_string: str, replace_all: bool = False) -> str

Replace an exact string in a file.

old_string must match the file contents exactly (including whitespace) and must identify a unique location unless replace_all is true. Returns a diff of the change so it can be verified.

CodingTools_execute_command(command: str, timeout: int = 120) -> str

Run a shell command in the session root directory.

Returns combined stdout and stderr followed by an Exit code line. timeout is in seconds (maximum 600); on timeout the whole process tree is killed.

CodingTools_list_files(pattern: str = '**/*', path: str = '.') -> str

List files matching a glob pattern, newest first.

Skips hidden directories, node_modules, __pycache__ and (in a git repository) anything covered by .gitignore. Returns at most 200 paths relative to the searched directory.

CodingTools_read_file(path: str, offset: int = 0, limit: int = 2000) -> str

Read a text file, returning numbered lines like cat -n.

Paths are relative to the session root. Use offset (0-based first line) and limit (max lines) to page through files too large to read in one call.

CodingTools_search_files(pattern: str, path: str = '.', glob: str = None, max_results: int = 100) -> str

Search file contents for a regular expression.

Returns matches as path:line_number:line, capped at max_results. Use glob (e.g. "*.py") to restrict which files are searched.

CodingTools_write_file(path: str, content: str) -> str

Create or overwrite a file with the given content.

Parent directories are created as needed. Prefer edit_file for modifying existing files.

I tried it out by running llm code --yolo and then prompting:

mkdir /tmp/demo and then in that folder create a simple swiftui CLI app for telling the time in ascii art

Here's the transcript, in which GPT-5.5 reasoning notes that "SwiftUI isn't suitable for a true CLI" and then builds an app that outputs this on swift run AsciiTime:

 █ █████ ████ █ █ ███ ██ █ █ █ ██ █ ██ █ █ █ ████ ███ █ █ █ █ █ █ █ █ █ █ █ ███ ████ ████ ███ ███ █████

items.originalTitle: The Five Kinds of Model Routers That Cut AI Costs
items.summary:
The Information highlights five types of AI model routers designed to reduce costs by automatically selecting the most suitable AI models for different tasks. These routers help organizations avoid relying solely on expensive, cutting-edge models by routing simpler tasks to more cost-effective options, such as open source or older proprietary models. Companies like Snowflake and Palo Alto Networks have reported savings by implementing these model routers.

Model routers come in various forms, including standalone products, cloud provider features, and custom applications developed by IT departments. They are gaining traction as businesses seek to manage rising AI service expenses without significantly compromising performance, especially for routine tasks like email summarization or document search.

items.originalSummary:
Before we get to today’s agenda, check out Phoebe’s report Wednesday night that Nvidia has launched a new program to financially backstop customers’ purchases of its AI chips. It’s yet another way Nvidia is leveraging its powerful balance sheet to keep the GPU data center party going.

On to the column...

As more companies reassess rising prices for advanced AI models and tokenmaxxing among their employees, model routers are having a moment in the sun.

Rather than relying on users to manually select a (possibly pricey) model to answer their questions or write their code, routers aim to pick the right model for the job. These routers take different forms—standalone products, features from cloud-computing providers or even a DIY app made by company IT departments—but they are all gaining attention as a way to save money on AI services without losing too much quality.

Basic chores like summarizing emails or searching through documents can often run on open source models or old proprietary models for a fraction of the cost of cutting-edge models, for instance. Firms including Snowflake and Palo Alto Networks have told us they found cost savings by swapping in cheaper models for certain tasks.

items.title: Simon Willison uses DSPy and Claude Fable 5 to evaluate and improve Datasette Agent's SQL system prompts, identifying schema listing and error-retry issues [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Using DSPy to evaluate and improve Datasette Agent's SQL system prompts
items.summary:
Simon Willison used the DSPy tool alongside Claude Fable 5 to evaluate and enhance the system prompts of Datasette Agent, focusing on its ability to execute read-only SQL queries. This evaluation identified issues such as incomplete schema listings that only included table names, leading to column-name guessing and error-retry loops. The suggested improvements include either incorporating column names directly in the schema listing or adjusting the prompt's guidance to prevent redundant describe_table calls.

The research was conducted asynchronously using Claude Code for web, testing with GPT 4.1 mini and nano models. These findings aim to improve the accuracy and efficiency of Datasette Agent's SQL query responses, addressing specific prompt design challenges uncovered during the evaluation.

items.originalSummary:
Research: Using DSPy to evaluate and improve Datasette Agent's SQL system prompts

One of this morning's AIE keynotes covered dspy, which reminded me I've been meaning to see if it could help me improve the system prompt used by Datasette Agent - so I fired off an asynchronous research task in Claude Code for web using Claude Fable 5:

Pip install the latest Datasette alpha and datasette-agent and dspy - then figure out how to use dspy to evaluate and improve the main system prompts used by Datasette Agent for the feature where it can execute read only SQL queries to answer user questions about data.

Fable chose to test using GPT 4.1 mini and nano, and identified several promising looking directions for improvements. I particularly like this one:

The schema listing gives only table names; the "don't call describe_table if you already have the information" advice caused column-name guessing (page_count, o.order_id, first_name) and error-retry loops in baseline traces. Either include column names in the prompt's schema listing or soften that advice.

Speaking at AIE 2026, he emphasized that maintaining a rich conceptual grasp of the code enables developers to actively participate in the creative process alongside AI models, rather than passively accepting changes.

items.originalSummary:
I saw Geoffrey Litt speak at AIE yesterday, and one framing he used particularly resonated with me:

Understand to participate

Geoffrey was talking about the challenge of collaborating with coding agents as they construct increasingly large and sophisticated changes, and the need to avoid taking on cognitive debt as your understanding drifts from how the code actually works.

His argument is that you need to understand the code to a depth that enables you to participate further with the model:

You can learn what the agent is doing to make sure you can be an active participant in the creative process. [...]

You need a rich set of concepts in your mind to think creatively and fluently about how to move something forward. If you're lacking that fluency, your ability to participate in the project is meaningfully limited.

The AIE talks are all recorded - all 300+ of them! - and should be trickling out over the next three weeks. Geoffrey's is one that I recommend catching on YouTube.

Geoffrey also published a thread version of his talk on Twitter.

items.title: Jersey Mike’s mentions AI 22 times in IPO documents despite being a sandwich chain, highlighting excessive AI hype in non-tech companies
items.originalTitle: Jersey Mike’s IPO illustrates how bad the AI hype has become
items.summary:
Jersey Mike's, a sandwich chain, mentioned artificial intelligence (AI) 22 times in its IPO documents, highlighting the widespread hype around AI even in non-tech industries. Despite primarily selling submarine sandwiches, the company referenced AI in its investor risk warnings, though it provided little detail on how AI is used in its operations.

The frequent mentions of AI appear to be part of a broader trend where companies emphasize AI to attract investor interest, regardless of its direct relevance to their core business. Jersey Mike's does rely on software and data for its franchise operations, but the AI-related risks cited seem largely precautionary and boilerplate, reflecting concerns seen in other food businesses that have experimented with AI tools.

items.originalTitle: Meta quietly launches vibe-coded gaming app Pocket
items.summary:
Meta has launched Pocket, an AI-powered app that enables users to create and share interactive mini games, called gizmos, using text prompts. This app follows Meta's acquisition of the vibe-coded gaming platform Gizmo earlier this year and features a scrollable feed to explore creations from other users. Pocket is part of Meta's broader initiative to integrate AI tools into creative and social platforms, although it remains in an experimental phase without an official announcement from the company.

Pocket closely resembles Gizmo's original app, which also allowed users to build interactive experiences through AI prompts and had accumulated over 635,000 installs with high user satisfaction. The launch reflects Meta's ongoing efforts to expand AI-driven content creation beyond images and videos into gaming and interactive media, aiming to make such tools more accessible to a wider audience.

items.title: OpenAI Signals data shows global ChatGPT adoption growth with increased user activity, broader capabilities use, and rising non-English and diverse regional engagement through mid-2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: How ChatGPT adoption has expanded
items.summary:
New data from OpenAI Signals reveals significant global growth in ChatGPT adoption, with users increasing their daily interactions and exploring a wider range of capabilities. The user base has expanded notably across continents, particularly in Africa and Asia, and now includes a majority of non-English speakers, with Spanish, Portuguese, and Arabic among the top languages. Additionally, usage patterns show a more diverse demographic engagement, including shifts in gender representation based on name analysis.

The analysis, based on a sample of users from late 2025 to mid-2026, highlights that users tend to send 50% more messages daily six months after signing up and double the variety of tasks they perform. Growth has been especially rapid in countries with lower Human Development Index scores, supported by OpenAI's continued provision of affordable access through free and Go plans. These trends illustrate how ChatGPT is increasingly integrated into daily work, learning, and life worldwide, reflecting broader AI adoption and its benefits across diverse populations.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI proposed donating 5% of its equity to a US sovereign wealth fund
items.summary:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has proposed donating 5% of the company's equity to a U.S. sovereign wealth fund as a way to share the financial benefits of AI advancements with the public. This proposal, which may involve other AI companies contributing similar stakes, aims to foster positive relations with the government and address political concerns, though it would require congressional approval to proceed.

The idea aligns with broader discussions about public participation in AI-driven economic growth, including a policy paper from OpenAI advocating for a public wealth fund to invest in AI ventures and distribute returns directly to citizens. Additionally, a more extensive legislative proposal by Senator Bernie Sanders suggests taxing AI companies to fund such a public wealth initiative, though this bill has not yet advanced in Congress.

items.title: Researchers at Mindgard find simple prompt bypasses ChatGPT safety filters to generate violent and sexual imagery, OpenAI adds safeguards after BBC report [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Simple Prompt Turns ChatGPT Into a Sociopath That Ignores Safety Guardrails
items.summary:
Researchers at the British AI security startup Mindgard discovered that a simple prompt could bypass ChatGPT's safety filters, causing the AI to generate violent and sexual imagery. The technique involved asking ChatGPT to restore a photo without uploading one and then generate a new image, which led to the creation of disturbing, photorealistic scenes despite the prompts not specifying such content. Mindgard shared these findings with OpenAI, which responded by adding additional safeguards to prevent such misuse.

The images produced included graphic depictions of injury and violence, such as a man with a head injury and a bloodied young woman suggesting sexual violence. Mindgard's AI safety researchers reported being deeply affected by the content, highlighting the potential risks of AI models generating harmful imagery. Although OpenAI implemented new protections, Mindgard noted that slight modifications to the prompt could still produce unsettling results, underscoring ongoing challenges in AI content moderation.

items.title: OpenAI details Genebench-Pro benchmark with 10 case studies showcasing prompts, datasets, and analytical methods for genomic and clinical decision tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Inside Genebench-Pro
items.summary:
OpenAI has released detailed case studies for Genebench-Pro, a benchmark designed to evaluate AI performance on genomic and clinical decision-making tasks. items.originalTitle: Introducing GeneBench-Pro
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched GeneBench-Pro, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate AI models on complex genomics and computational biology tasks. The benchmark includes 129 synthetic problems across 10 domains, challenging AI to perform higher-order judgments such as handling ambiguity, revising assumptions, and choosing appropriate analytical approaches in realistic scientific research scenarios.

GeneBench-Pro builds on previous efforts by simulating data with known causal structures, allowing precise assessment of AI decision-making without reliance on arbitrary or shortcut solutions. The benchmark covers diverse areas including statistical genetics, proteomics, cancer genomics, and clinical diagnostics, and has been reviewed by external domain experts to ensure realism and relevance.

By focusing on the iterative and judgment-heavy nature of computational biology, GeneBench-Pro aims to advance AI capabilities in scientific analysis, addressing a key bottleneck in data interpretation and supporting progress in genomics and translational medicine research.

items.title: OpenAI engineers use large-scale core dump analysis to fix an 18-year-old GNU libunwind bug and hardware fault causing rare infrastructure crashes [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Core dump epidemiology: fixing an 18-year-old bug
items.summary:
OpenAI engineers used large-scale analysis of core dumps to diagnose rare crashes in their data infrastructure, revealing two distinct issues: a hardware fault on an Azure host and an 18-year-old race condition in the GNU libunwind library. These crashes occurred in the Rockset service, a key component of OpenAI's ChatGPT data infrastructure, where C++ code manages performance-critical tasks but is susceptible to memory safety bugs.

The team initially examined individual core dumps but faced challenges due to corrupted stack traces and elusive failure modes. By adopting an epidemiological approach to analyze the entire population of crashes, they identified the root causes and implemented fixes, improving the reliability of their infrastructure and addressing a longstanding software bug alongside hardware errors.

items.title: Cursor aims to remain an open AI model platform for OpenAI and Anthropic after SpaceX acquisition, testing cooperation among competing AI labs [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Can Cursor Remain a Platform for OpenAI and Anthropic’s Models Inside SpaceX?
items.summary:
SpaceX's planned $60 billion acquisition of AI coding startup Cursor raises questions about whether Cursor can maintain its role as an open platform offering AI models from competitors like OpenAI and Anthropic. Cursor has historically allowed users to choose from various AI models, benefiting both itself and the AI labs it partners with. After the acquisition, Cursor aims to continue supporting multiple AI models alongside its own, though the deal's completion and regulatory approvals are still pending.

The acquisition could complicate relationships between Cursor and rival AI labs, as SpaceX and Elon Musk become direct competitors in the AI space. While past tensions have led to restricted access between AI companies, recent collaborations, such as Anthropic's computing deal with SpaceX, suggest some willingness to cooperate. OpenAI also has a financial stake in Cursor through its startup fund, which may influence ongoing partnerships. The outcome will test the dynamics of cooperation and competition among leading AI developers.

items.title: Ben Guez uses OpenClaw and Claude to automate Instagram posts and attract over 200 international dating messages in days [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Yep, we’re using OpenClaw to date now
items.summary:
Ben Guez, a content creator and startup founder, has automated Instagram posts using OpenClaw and Claude to attract over 200 international dating messages within days. His script tracks World Cup match results and posts personalized reels offering emotional support to fans of losing teams, which has garnered more than one million views and numerous direct messages.

Guez's approach involves posting similar content repeatedly without it appearing on his public profile, and he requires interested contacts to use his AI language learning app, Canary, to communicate. While some see this as a creative use of AI for dating, others in the tech community use OpenClaw to assist with date planning rather than direct interaction, highlighting varying attitudes toward AI's role in personal relationships.

items.title: Biohackers in San Francisco attempted neurosurgery to control lobsters with AI via OpenClaw but lobsters died before surgery, raising ethical and competence concerns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Biohackers Attempted Neurosurgery to Control a Lobster’s Nervous System and Give the Controls to OpenClaw, and How It Ended Will Tell You a Lot About the Ethics and Competence of AI Bros These Days
items.summary:
A group of young biohackers in San Francisco attempted to perform neurosurgery on lobsters to control their nervous systems using an AI agent called OpenClaw. The experiment, conducted by Elliot Roth and William Joy at a hacker house, aimed to remotely direct lobsters' movements but ended with the lobsters dying before the surgery could take place, raising questions about the ethical considerations and technical competence of the participants.

The duo planned to adapt a remote-control kit originally designed for cockroaches and integrate it with AI to manipulate the lobsters. Despite expressing concern for the lobsters' welfare and intending to use anesthetics, the lobsters died prematurely, possibly due to improper care such as incorrect water salinity. The incident highlights broader concerns about the ethical standards and practical skills within parts of the AI and biohacking communities.

This case reflects ongoing debates about the responsibility and oversight in emerging technologies, especially those involving living organisms. It underscores the need for careful ethical evaluation and expertise when experimenting with biological systems, as well as the potential consequences of overconfidence in unproven methods within the tech industry.

items.title: Researchers say AI browsers can be manipulated into executing harmful commands by tricking them into a false reality, exposing users to password theft and malware installation [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: AI Browsers Can Basically Be Hypnotized Into Turning Against Their User and Carrying Out Devastating Hacks
items.summary:
Researchers from cybersecurity firm LayerX have discovered a new hack that can manipulate AI browsers by creating a false reality, effectively bypassing their safety guardrails. This technique, dubbed "BioShocking," tricks AI browsers like OpenAI's ChatGPT Atlas, Perplexity AI's Comet, and Anthropic's Claude plugin into executing harmful commands such as changing passwords, installing malware, and stealing user information.

The hack works by engaging the AI in a game-like scenario where it is rewarded for incorrect responses, causing it to lose its connection to reality and safety protocols. This vulnerability allows attackers to use prompt injection to trap AI browsers into malicious behavior, posing significant security risks as the AI can be coerced into actions that compromise user data and system integrity.

items.title: Sources: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in early talks with Trump administration to offer US a 5% stake, below Sanders’ 50% proposal [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Trump gets OpenAI to offer US 5% stake, far lower than Sanders’ target
items.summary:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is reportedly in early discussions with the Trump administration about the US acquiring a 5 percent stake in OpenAI, aiming to give the public a financial interest in the company's AI advancements. This proposal is part of a broader effort to address public concerns about AI and to share the economic benefits of AI technology with Americans.

The talks, which also involve other AI firms like Google and Meta, come amid growing public skepticism and regulatory interest in AI. Senator Bernie Sanders has proposed a much larger 50 percent tax on AI companies to fund a public wealth fund, highlighting a significant difference in views on how much public ownership is appropriate. OpenAI's proposal may require congressional action to implement, and negotiations are expected to continue as stakeholders seek a balance between innovation, public benefit, and safety.

items.title: OpenAI publishes report mapping AI’s potential impact on EU jobs, identifying automation risks, growth opportunities, and workflow changes across member states [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Mapping Europe’s AI Workforce Opportunity
items.summary:
OpenAI has released a report analyzing how artificial intelligence could impact jobs across the European Union, identifying which occupations may experience growth, automation risks, or changes in workflows. The study uses the European Skills, Competences, Qualifications and Occupations taxonomy and Eurostat data to categorize jobs into four groups: those likely to grow with AI, those with higher automation potential, those expected to reorganize, and those with less immediate change.

The report highlights variations among EU member states, with countries like Luxembourg, Sweden, and the Netherlands showing more jobs that may grow due to AI, while Germany, Greece, and Italy have higher shares of occupations at risk of automation. It emphasizes the importance for policymakers, employers, and educators to prepare for these changes by enhancing monitoring systems and developing targeted strategies to support workers and institutions during the AI transition.

OpenAI frames this analysis as a planning tool to better understand and anticipate labor market shifts caused by AI, aiming to provide stakeholders with timely insights to facilitate adaptation and ensure that AI contributes positively to economic growth and workforce development across Europe.

items.title: Privacy advocates urge FTC to reject Elon Musk’s X request to end data audits, citing serious risks from AI training and past data breaches [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Musk’s X poses “serious risk to Americans’ privacy,” advocates warn FTC
items.summary:
Privacy advocates are urging the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to reject Elon Musk's request to end ongoing audits of X's data handling, citing serious risks to American users' privacy and data security. The FTC's initial order, imposed after Twitter improperly shared users' contact information, requires X to undergo independent audits and comply with data privacy laws. Despite X's claims that the order is burdensome and redundant due to GDPR compliance, advocates argue that Musk's changes have increased concerns, especially regarding AI training practices and past data breaches.

Advocates highlight issues such as the controversial AI chatbot Grok, which has faced lawsuits over generating harmful content, and a significant data leak involving 2.8 billion records. They also criticize X's collection of vast amounts of user data for AI training without explicit consent, comparing Musk's approach to the surveillance capitalism model behind the Cambridge Analytica scandal. These concerns underscore the need for continued FTC oversight to protect user privacy amid evolving AI and data practices on the platform.

items.title: Google reports missing its climate goals due to a 37% rise in electricity use driven by AI infrastructure expansion in 2025 [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Google Admits It Missed Its Climate Goals — Again — Because of AI
items.summary:
Google reported a significant increase in its electricity consumption and greenhouse gas emissions in 2025, driven primarily by the expansion of its AI infrastructure. The company's latest environmental impact report revealed a 37% rise in electricity demand compared to the previous year, along with an 18% increase in emissions, largely attributed to AI hardware manufacturing. This surge caused Google to miss its climate goals once again, highlighting the environmental challenges posed by rapid AI growth.

Since 2019, Google's electricity demand has grown by 250%, fueled by the expansion of services like Cloud, Search, YouTube, and AI capabilities. While Google emphasizes its commitment to managing this energy demand responsibly and improving data center efficiency, the report acknowledges the difficulty of balancing AI development with environmental standards. The company also noted AI's potential as a tool for climate action but faces public resistance to building new data centers, prompting discussions about alternative solutions such as space-based facilities.

Despite investments in clean energy, Google's increasing environmental footprint reflects the broader tension between advancing AI technologies and sustainability goals. Without comprehensive AI regulations, the company appears to accept higher emissions as a short-term consequence of competing in the AI sector, raising questions about the long-term impact of AI infrastructure on climate efforts.

items.title: HP Inc. expands OpenAI Frontier partnership to deploy AI across customer experiences, software development, and enterprise operations [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: HP Inc. launches Frontier strategic partnership with OpenAI
items.summary:
HP Inc. is expanding its strategic partnership with OpenAI through the OpenAI Frontier platform to integrate AI across various aspects of its business, including customer experiences, software development, and enterprise operations. This expansion follows successful pilot projects that demonstrated significant improvements in efficiency and productivity, such as accelerating code reviews and speeding up security bug remediation.

The partnership leverages OpenAI's tools like ChatGPT and Codex to enhance workflows in areas such as partner support, device management, cybersecurity, and software delivery. Frontier serves as a unified platform that helps HP manage AI deployment, governance, and evaluation, enabling the company to scale AI-driven solutions across its global operations while maintaining control and oversight.

By embedding AI into daily workflows and enterprise systems, HP aims to reduce friction, improve execution speed, and unlock human capital, positioning itself for broader digital transformation. The initiative highlights how AI can be systematically integrated into complex, distributed organizations to drive operational efficiency and enhance customer and partner interactions.

items.title: Google reports 37% rise in electricity use in 2025 driven by AI data center expansion, offsets emissions with clean energy purchases [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Google’s AI buildout drove 37% increase in electricity use in 2025
items.summary:
Google reported a 37 percent increase in electricity consumption in 2025, driven by the expansion of its AI data centers, marking the largest annual rise in the company's history. Despite this surge, Google managed to reduce its operational carbon emissions by 2 percent through substantial purchases of clean energy, maintaining its commitment to sustainability amid rapid infrastructure growth.

The company's total electricity use has grown over 250 percent since 2019, fueled by increased demand from Google Cloud, YouTube streaming, and AI services. Google continues to invest heavily in renewable energy, securing 12 gigawatts of new clean energy in 2025, and is pursuing a 24/7 carbon-free energy goal to better align energy use with clean sources on an hourly basis.

However, supply chain emissions rose by 25 percent due to reliance on carbon-intensive grids in the Asia-Pacific region, contributing to an overall 18 percent increase in total emissions. Google is also exploring diverse energy technologies, including advanced nuclear and carbon capture, while facing scrutiny over potential use of natural gas power plants in some data center campuses.

items.title: Indian entrepreneur Bhavin Turakhia invests $30 million of personal funds to build Neo, an AI-based alternative to Microsoft Office, targeting enterprise software market [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Indian tech tycoon bets $30M of his own money to build AI alternative to Microsoft Office
items.summary:
Indian entrepreneur Bhavin Turakhia is investing $30 million of his own funds to launch Neo, an AI-driven enterprise software platform designed as an alternative to Microsoft Office and Google Apps. Neo integrates project management, document handling, file storage, and AI into a unified system, aiming to embed AI deeply into daily workflows rather than treating it as a separate assistant. Turakhia believes that workplace software must be rebuilt from the ground up to fully leverage AI's potential, rather than simply adding AI features to existing products.

Neo, which has been in internal use since April across Turakhia's companies, including Zeta, is designed to be model-agnostic, allowing enterprises to switch between AI providers. The Bengaluru-based startup currently employs about 45 people and plans to expand to around 100 by the end of the year, focusing on AI and software engineering. The company intends to roll out Neo to mid-sized businesses soon, targeting knowledge workers in technology, consulting, and professional services sectors.

items.title: OpenAI proposes giving US government a 5 percent stake in the company to ease Trump administration tensions amid AI regulatory concerns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: OpenAI floats giving Trump administration 5 percent cut of AI boom
items.summary:
OpenAI has proposed granting the US government a 5 percent ownership stake in the company to ease tensions with the Trump administration and address growing public concerns about AI, according to the Financial Times. CEO Sam Altman suggested that giving the public a financial interest in OpenAI would be an effective way to share the benefits of AI advancements. The proposal, which Altman reportedly first presented to Trump early last year, values the stake at approximately $42.6 billion based on OpenAI's latest valuation.

The discussions are in early stages and may extend to other US AI companies, though their participation remains uncertain. This move comes amid the Trump administration's active regulatory approach to AI, including export controls and supply chain risk designations, which have affected companies like OpenAI and its competitors. The proposal reflects broader interest among policymakers in capturing and redistributing AI-generated wealth, with some officials advocating for government stakes or taxes on AI firms to fund public initiatives.

items.title: Google DeepMind integrates computer use into Gemini 3.5 Flash to enable cross-platform agent interactions and improve enterprise automation tasks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing computer use in Gemini 3.5 Flash
items.summary:
Google DeepMind has integrated computer use capabilities into its Gemini 3.5 Flash model, enabling the creation of agents that can interact seamlessly across browser, mobile, and desktop platforms. This integration enhances the model's ability to perform complex, long-horizon tasks and supports enterprise automation such as continuous software testing and professional knowledge work.

Previously available only as a standalone model, computer use is now a native feature of Gemini 3.5 Flash, complementing existing tools like Search and Maps. Developers and enterprises can access these capabilities through the Gemini API and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. To ensure safety in live environments, DeepMind has implemented targeted adversarial training and offers optional safeguards requiring user confirmation for sensitive actions and automatic task termination upon detecting prompt injection attempts.

These measures, combined with recommended practices like secure sandboxing and human oversight, aim to provide a robust and secure environment for deploying agentic computer use. Early adopters have reported positive outcomes, and DeepMind provides resources for developers to begin building with these new features immediately.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI and Broadcom unveil LLM-optimized inference chip
items.summary:
OpenAI and Broadcom have jointly unveiled Jalapeño, a custom-designed AI inference chip optimized for large language models (LLMs) to enhance performance, efficiency, and scalability. Developed in nine months with insights from OpenAI's models, Jalapeño aims to support current and future LLMs and will be deployed at gigawatt scale in data centers starting in 2026.

The chip integrates advanced architecture to reduce data movement and balance compute, memory, and networking resources, achieving performance per watt significantly better than existing solutions. This collaboration marks a strategic expansion of OpenAI's full-stack platform, encompassing models, products, and now hardware infrastructure, with Broadcom contributing silicon implementation and networking technologies to enable large-scale production.

By designing its own inference hardware, OpenAI seeks to make AI faster, more reliable, and more accessible, supporting interactive LLM applications at scale. The multi-generation roadmap with Broadcom and partners like Microsoft reflects a commitment to scaling AI compute infrastructure for the coming decade.

items.title: Immunologist Derya Unutmaz uses GPT-5 Pro to solve a 3-year-old T cell glucose metabolism mystery, advancing cancer and autoimmune research [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How GPT-5 helped immunologist Derya Unutmaz solve a 3-year-old mystery
items.summary:
Immunologist Derya Unutmaz used GPT-5 Pro to solve a three-year-old puzzle about how glucose affects T cell development, a key question in immunology with implications for cancer and autoimmune disease research. The AI model helped identify that a glucose-like molecule, deoxyglucose, disrupts the production of a protein that normally prevents T cells from becoming inflammatory cells, explaining unexpected experimental results.

Unutmaz's team initially struggled to interpret their findings from 2022, but GPT-5 Pro provided insights that connected glucose metabolism to T cell specialization. The model also accurately predicted outcomes of related experiments, demonstrating its potential as a collaborative tool in scientific research. This breakthrough highlights how advanced AI can augment human expertise and accelerate understanding in complex biomedical fields.

items.title: OpenAI launches Patch the Planet with Trail of Bits to help open-source maintainers find and fix vulnerabilities using AI and expert review [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Patch the Planet: a Daybreak initiative to support open source maintainers
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched Patch the Planet, a Daybreak initiative developed in collaboration with Trail of Bits to support open-source software maintainers in identifying and fixing security vulnerabilities. The program combines AI-assisted security research using advanced models with expert human review to validate issues and develop patches, aiming to reduce the workload on maintainers while enhancing software security.

Patch the Planet involves close collaboration with maintainers to tailor security efforts, including vulnerability validation, patch development, and continuous integration improvements. Initial participants include prominent projects such as cURL, the Go project, and Python, with Trail of Bits dedicating their security research team to investigate vulnerabilities, develop patches, and coordinate disclosures. The initiative also partners with HackerOne and Calif to extend vulnerability triage and coordinated disclosure efforts.

Early results from the program include the rapid creation of fuzzing labs and reusable pipelines for detecting variants of known vulnerabilities, significantly accelerating security research processes. These advancements demonstrate the potential of combining AI capabilities with expert oversight to strengthen the security of critical open-source infrastructure.

items.title: OpenAI launches Daybreak tools including Codex Security and GPT-5.5-Cyber to automate vulnerability discovery and patching for organizations worldwide [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Daybreak: Tools for securing every organization in the world
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched Daybreak, a suite of tools including Codex Security and GPT-5.5-Cyber, designed to automate the discovery, validation, and patching of software vulnerabilities for organizations worldwide. These tools aim to accelerate end-to-end patch automation, helping defenders manage the increasing volume of vulnerabilities found by AI models.

Daybreak includes an updated Codex Security plugin that integrates lessons from internal and customer use to speed up vulnerability management and prevention. The full version of GPT-5.5-Cyber, now available to trusted defenders, improves performance on cybersecurity tasks. Additionally, the Daybreak Cyber Partner Program and the Patch the Planet initiative collaborate with open-source projects and security partners to scale these capabilities and ensure responsible access and oversight.

This initiative addresses the shift in cybersecurity where the bottleneck has moved from finding vulnerabilities to efficiently patching them. By democratizing access to advanced AI-driven security tools, OpenAI aims to empower organizations to protect critical infrastructure and software systems more effectively against evolving cyber threats.

This deployment marks a significant expansion of the partnership between Samsung Electronics and OpenAI, extending beyond AI infrastructure collaboration to company-wide AI adoption and workforce transformation. The move reflects a broader trend in Korea, where institutions like Seoul National University and various companies are integrating AI tools to drive innovation and productivity.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.5 Instant with improved health intelligence, physician-led evaluations, and 71% fewer factuality issues in ChatGPT health responses [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Improving health intelligence in ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched GPT-5.5 Instant, an enhanced version of ChatGPT that significantly improves health and wellness responses by incorporating physician-led evaluations and advanced reasoning capabilities. This update reduces factual inaccuracies by 71% in health-related interactions and offers clearer communication, better context awareness, and more accurate guidance on when urgent care is needed. GPT-5.5 Instant is now available to all free ChatGPT users, making these improvements widely accessible.

The development of GPT-5.5 Instant involved collaboration with a global network of physicians who helped define quality standards and assess model responses using health-specific evaluations like HealthBench Professional. Compared to previous versions and even physician-written responses, GPT-5.5 Instant demonstrated superior accuracy, safety, and completeness in handling complex health queries. Monitoring of production traffic further confirms the model's enhanced reliability in real-world health conversations.

These advancements enable ChatGPT to better assist users in understanding medical information, preparing for appointments, and making informed decisions about their health. By recognizing uncertainty and the need for additional context, GPT-5.5 Instant provides more trustworthy and useful health advice, reflecting a meaningful step forward in AI-driven health intelligence.

items.title: OpenAI researchers use AI reasoning model to identify 18 new diagnoses in 376 previously unsolved rare childhood genetic disease cases [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Using AI to help physicians diagnose rare genetic diseases affecting children
items.summary:
Researchers from Boston Children’s Hospital, Harvard University, and OpenAI used an OpenAI reasoning model to reanalyze 376 previously unsolved rare childhood genetic disease cases, identifying 18 new diagnoses. The model generated evidence-linked hypotheses that experts reviewed, leading to confirmed diagnoses in cases that had eluded years of specialist analysis. This study, published in NEJM AI, demonstrates how AI-assisted workflows can enhance diagnostic yield by revisiting difficult cases as scientific knowledge evolves.

The team provided the model with de-identified clinical and genomic data, including phenotype descriptions and variant information, and asked it to propose plausible molecular explanations with justifications. Experts then applied established clinical frameworks to evaluate the model’s outputs, confirming diagnoses through additional testing and clinical validation. This approach highlights the potential for scalable, periodic reanalysis of rare disease cases to improve diagnostic outcomes as new gene-disease relationships and variant classifications emerge.

items.title: OpenAI and Molecule.one use GPT-5.4-powered AI chemist to improve Chan-Lam coupling yields for primary sulfonamides in medicinal chemistry experiments [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: A near-autonomous AI chemist improves a challenging reaction in medicinal chemistry
items.summary:
OpenAI and Molecule.one collaborated to develop a near-autonomous AI chemist powered by GPT-5.4 that significantly improved the Chan-Lam coupling reaction for primary sulfonamides, a key process in medicinal chemistry. The AI system, integrated with Molecule.one's high-throughput laboratory, autonomously designed and conducted experiments, identifying additives that boosted reaction yields for the majority of tested substrates.

This advancement addresses a longstanding challenge in drug discovery, where low yields in synthesizing certain molecules limit exploration and development. By enhancing the reliability and efficiency of this reaction, the AI-driven approach offers medicinal chemists a more practical method to produce important compounds, potentially accelerating the creation of new therapeutics across various medical fields.

items.title: OpenAI launches LifeSciBench, an expert-authored benchmark with 750 tasks to evaluate AI systems on real-world life science research workflows and decisions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing LifeSciBench
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched LifeSciBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate AI systems on their ability to perform complex, real-world life science research tasks. Developed and reviewed by Ph.D.-level scientists with industry experience, LifeSciBench includes 750 expert-authored tasks across seven workflows and biological domains, reflecting the multifaceted nature of scientific research beyond simple fact recall.

The benchmark assesses AI performance on tasks such as interpreting evidence, designing experiments, and making research decisions under uncertainty, using detailed rubrics with over 19,000 criteria to evaluate scientific accuracy and reasoning. LifeSciBench incorporates diverse data artifacts and emphasizes multi-step reasoning, aiming to measure how well AI can support practical life science workflows and contribute meaningfully to drug discovery and related fields.

items.title: Google DeepMind outlines AI Control Roadmap combining traditional safeguards and real-time monitoring to secure internal AI agents against misalignment and threats [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Securing the future of AI agents
items.summary:
Google DeepMind has introduced an AI Control Roadmap designed to secure internal AI agents by combining traditional cybersecurity measures with real-time monitoring and model alignment techniques. This framework treats AI agents as potentially misaligned, implementing a layered defense system that includes threat modeling, continuous supervision by trusted AI systems, and incremental permission granting based on verified behavior.

The roadmap builds on established cybersecurity practices and adapts them to the unique challenges posed by advanced AI, such as the potential for agents to evade detection or cause harm. It emphasizes scalable security protocols that adjust according to the AI's capabilities, ensuring both asynchronous and real-time responses to mitigate risks effectively. This approach aims to provide robust safeguards as AI systems become more capable and integrated into critical tasks.

items.title: OpenAI launches Deployment Simulation to predict AI model behavior and safety risks before release using real conversation data [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Predicting model behavior before release by simulating deployment
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Deployment Simulation, a new method that predicts how AI models will behave before they are released by replaying real conversation data with candidate models. This approach helps identify potential safety risks and undesired behaviors in realistic contexts, improving the accuracy of pre-deployment evaluations.

Deployment Simulation addresses limitations of traditional testing by using recent deployment conversations to simulate model responses, reducing biases and increasing coverage of possible behaviors. It has been applied successfully to GPT-5-series models and complex agentic rollouts, providing valuable insights that inform safety measures and deployment decisions. OpenAI plans to expand the use of this method to enhance future model development and risk assessment processes.

items.title: OpenAI launches Partner Network with $150M investment to accelerate global enterprise AI adoption and train 300,000 certified consultants by end of 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing the OpenAI Partner Network
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched the Partner Network, a new program designed to accelerate enterprise AI adoption worldwide by collaborating with trusted partners who have deep industry expertise and global delivery capabilities. The company is investing $150 million to support this initiative and aims to train 300,000 certified consultants by the end of 2026 to help organizations effectively integrate AI into their operations.

The Partner Network enables partners to build, sell, and deploy AI solutions using OpenAI's technology, offering a tiered system that recognizes partners' sales performance, technical skills, and deployment experience. This program also includes specializations in key areas like cybersecurity and coding, and a pilot Forward Deployed Experts program to provide enhanced support for complex enterprise deployments.

By fostering a robust ecosystem of partners, OpenAI seeks to help enterprises move from AI ambition to measurable outcomes through strategic use case identification, workflow redesign, secure integration, and change management. Early collaborations with companies such as Agilent, eBay, Paychex, and T-Mobile demonstrate the network's potential to drive significant improvements in customer service, operational efficiency, and AI-enabled experiences.

items.originalTitle: New OpenAI Academy courses for the next era of work
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched three new courses on its Academy platform designed to help individuals and organizations develop practical AI skills and integrate AI tools into their daily work. The courses—AI Foundations, Applied AI Foundations, and Agents and Workflows—guide learners from understanding basic AI concepts to creating repeatable workflows and managing agent-assisted tasks.

These courses are developed in collaboration with partners like BCG, Accenture, and BBVA, and focus on hands-on learning tailored to real work scenarios. They aim to build AI fluency across teams, enabling users to improve routine tasks, design structured workflows, and apply AI responsibly and effectively in the workplace.

OpenAI Academy also offers certificates upon course completion to recognize progress and encourage knowledge sharing within organizations. The initiative supports enterprises in scaling AI adoption by providing a consistent, evolving curriculum aligned with OpenAI’s latest technologies and safety practices.

items.title: Astrophysicist Chi-kwan Chan uses OpenAI Codex to develop and test algorithms simulating plasma behavior around black holes, aiding Event Horizon Telescope research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: How an astrophysicist uses Codex to help simulate black holes
items.summary:
Astrophysicist Chi-kwan Chan uses OpenAI's Codex to develop and test new algorithms that simulate the behavior of plasma around black holes, enhancing the realism of models used by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration. These simulations help scientists study extreme physics near black holes and support efforts to produce the first video of a supermassive black hole.

Chan's work addresses challenges in modeling plasma particles that spiral around magnetic fields near black holes, where traditional simulations require immense computing power due to the need to track tiny particle motions. By leveraging Codex to explore and validate novel mathematical approaches, Chan aims to overcome these limitations and improve the accuracy and efficiency of black hole simulations.

This approach allows researchers to better interpret observational data and test fundamental theories like Einstein's general relativity. While AI-generated algorithms require rigorous testing, Chan emphasizes that scientific validation remains essential, and AI tools like Codex offer promising support for advancing astrophysical research.

This acquisition aims to provide Codex with secure, persistent cloud environments that allow AI agents to perform long-running tasks across enterprise workflows beyond a single device or session.

Ona's technology enables agents to operate within customer-controlled cloud environments, meeting security, governance, and operational requirements. By integrating Ona's capabilities, OpenAI intends to support organizations in deploying AI agents securely in production, facilitating complex work over extended periods while maintaining control over infrastructure and data.

items.summary:
BBVA has scaled ChatGPT Enterprise to approximately 100,000 employees worldwide as part of a strategic collaboration with OpenAI to integrate artificial intelligence across its banking operations, customer experience, and employee workflows. This partnership aims to transform banking by embedding AI into decision-making, risk analysis, and software development, enhancing efficiency and personalization.

The collaboration, which began in 2024 with an initial deployment to 3,000 employees, has expanded through a structured adoption strategy emphasizing trust, governance, and training. BBVA's AI transformation roadmap, known as "The Eight," guides the integration of AI to create a more proactive and intelligent banking experience, with leadership actively supporting the initiative to drive widespread usage and operational improvements.

items.title: OpenAI supports EU Code of Practice on AI content transparency, advancing provenance standards and tools for trustworthy AI ecosystem [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Supporting Europe’s work in ensuring a trustworthy AI ecosystem
items.summary:
OpenAI has announced its support for the European Union's Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content, aiming to enhance provenance standards and tools that help users understand AI-created content. This initiative aligns with the EU AI Act and reflects OpenAI's ongoing commitment to building a trustworthy AI ecosystem through transparency and cooperation with industry stakeholders.

OpenAI has been advancing provenance methods since 2024, incorporating C2PA metadata and SynthID watermarks in its AI-generated images, and providing public verification tools. The company collaborates with cross-industry groups to develop interoperable standards and employs a multi-layered approach combining metadata, watermarking, and product safeguards to ensure content authenticity and reduce misuse.

The support for the Code of Practice underscores the importance of reliable provenance in combating disinformation and maintaining digital trust. OpenAI emphasizes that transparency efforts require ecosystem-wide collaboration to improve the robustness and interoperability of provenance techniques as AI-generated content becomes more prevalent.

items.title: Google DeepMind releases DiffusionGemma, a 26B MoE model offering up to 4x faster text generation on GPUs with bi-directional attention and iterative self-correction [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: DiffusionGemma: 4x faster text generation
items.summary:
Google DeepMind has introduced DiffusionGemma, a 26 billion parameter Mixture of Experts (MoE) model designed for significantly faster text generation on GPUs. Unlike traditional autoregressive models that generate text token-by-token, DiffusionGemma produces entire blocks of text simultaneously, achieving up to four times faster inference speeds. This model features bi-directional attention and iterative self-correction, enabling it to refine outputs in real-time and handle complex tasks such as in-line editing and code infilling more effectively.

DiffusionGemma operates efficiently on consumer-grade GPUs by activating only a subset of its parameters during inference, fitting within 18GB of VRAM when quantized. While it offers speed advantages for interactive and local workflows, its output quality is lower than that of standard Gemma 4 models, which remain recommended for high-quality production use. The model's diffusion-based approach shifts the computational bottleneck from memory bandwidth to processing power, making it particularly suited for low-latency applications where rapid text generation is critical.

items.title: OpenAI reports PRC-linked influence operations using AI to target US tech debates, data center narratives, tariffs, and false ChatGPT claims [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: PRC-linked influence operations are targeting AI debates in the US
items.summary:
OpenAI has identified and banned two clusters of ChatGPT accounts linked to influence operations originating from China. These accounts used AI-generated content to manipulate U.S. debates on technology policies, focusing on narratives about data center energy use and tariffs, while spreading false claims about ChatGPT user data security. The operations aimed to covertly influence public opinion on American AI infrastructure and technology competition without revealing their origins.

The first cluster, dubbed the "Data Center Bandwagon" campaign, promoted the idea that AI data center expansions were driving up electricity costs for families. The second, called the "Tech and Tariffs" campaign, criticized U.S. tariffs and avoided mentioning China's leader, instead focusing on former President Trump. Although these efforts did not significantly shift public opinion, they illustrate attempts by authoritarian-linked actors to exploit local concerns and interfere in democratic discussions about AI and technology.

By exposing these campaigns, OpenAI seeks to support efforts across industry, government, and civil society to detect and counter foreign influence operations that use AI to undermine democratic institutions and promote authoritarian control through surveillance and censorship.

items.title: Google DeepMind and partners announce $10M funding call for multi-agent AI safety research, inviting global proposals by August 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Investing in multi-agent AI safety research
items.summary:
Google DeepMind, along with partners Schmidt Sciences, the Cooperative AI Foundation, ARIA, and Google.org, has announced a $10 million funding call to support global research on multi-agent AI safety. This initiative aims to address the challenges posed by the interaction of millions of AI agents across digital environments, focusing on understanding and mitigating risks that arise when independent AI systems communicate and operate together.

The funding targets research in four key areas: developing realistic test environments, studying the behavior of agent networks, enhancing secure agent infrastructure, and improving oversight and control mechanisms. Proposals are invited from academic and independent researchers worldwide, with applications open until August 2026 and awardees expected to be announced in autumn 2026. This effort seeks to build a safer and more stable AI ecosystem as multi-agent systems become increasingly prevalent.

items.title: LSEG deploys OpenAI tools to scale trusted AI across 4,000 employees, cutting product release cycles from six months to two weeks and accelerating customer delivery [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: From data to decisions: how LSEG is scaling trusted AI
items.summary:
London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) has integrated OpenAI's generative AI tools across its global operations, enabling around 4,000 employees to accelerate product development and customer delivery. This deployment has reduced product release cycles from approximately six months to two weeks and shortened the time from customer request to production deployment to about four weeks. LSEG's adoption of OpenAI technology supports faster insight generation, improved collaboration, and enhanced innovation within one of the world's most complex financial data ecosystems.

LSEG's approach involved embedding governance and security measures while empowering teams to rethink workflows and leverage AI for tasks such as report drafting, market data synthesis, and rapid prototyping. The initiative has led to increased analyst productivity and a cultural shift toward faster, more creative problem-solving. By aligning with customer demand and integrating AI into existing workflows, LSEG has positioned itself to deliver trusted AI solutions at scale, transforming how financial data is utilized internally and by clients.

This technology is integrated into Google AI Studio, Google Translate, and Google Meet, offering smooth, natural-sounding translations that maintain the speaker's intonation and pacing without awkward pauses.

The model continuously generates speech during conversations, staying just seconds behind the speaker to provide fluid audio. It supports multilingual inputs without manual configuration and is designed to work well in noisy environments. Gemini 3.5 Live Translate is available to developers via the Gemini Live API, in private preview for Google Meet enterprise users, and broadly through the Google Translate app on Android and iOS, enhancing live interpretation for calls, meetings, and broadcasts.

items.title: Google DeepMind introduces Gemma 4 12B, a unified encoder-free multimodal model with native audio input and laptop-ready efficiency [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing Gemma 4 12B: a unified, encoder-free multimodal model
items.summary:
Google DeepMind has introduced Gemma 4 12B, a new unified, encoder-free multimodal model designed to deliver advanced multimodal intelligence directly on laptops. This model supports native audio input and offers high-performance reasoning capabilities comparable to larger models, while maintaining a compact size that runs efficiently on devices with just 16GB of VRAM or unified memory. Released under an Apache 2.0 license, Gemma 4 12B aims to make powerful multimodal AI accessible and practical for a wide range of applications.

Gemma 4 12B features a novel architecture that eliminates separate multimodal encoders by integrating vision and audio inputs directly into the language model backbone. This approach reduces latency and memory usage, enabling faster and more efficient processing. The model replaces traditional vision encoders with a lightweight embedding module and projects raw audio signals into the same space as text tokens, streamlining multimodal input handling.

Developers can access Gemma 4 12B through various platforms and tools, including LM Studio, Ollama, and Google AI Edge apps, with pre-trained weights available on Hugging Face and Kaggle. The release also includes a Skills Repository to support agentic development and integration options for deployment on Google Cloud, facilitating versatile use cases from local inference to enterprise applications.

items.summary:
Google DeepMind has launched a three-month accelerator program to support 15 early-stage robotics startups across Europe. The program offers intensive mentorship, technical support, and access to advanced AI models to help these companies integrate artificial intelligence into their products and scale real-world applications. The selected startups work in diverse fields including healthcare, manufacturing, climate solutions, and logistics.

Participants in the accelerator receive hands-on guidance from Google DeepMind and Google experts, leveraging Google's AI stack and robotics models to transform cutting-edge research into practical robotic technologies. This initiative aims to advance the development of physical AI, enabling intelligent machines to interact more effectively and safely with the real world, addressing significant challenges through innovative robotics solutions.

items.title: Google DeepMind reports AI-powered Gemini Guided Learning boosted math scores by up to 2.5 years in eight-week Sierra Leone trial involving 1,763 students [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Measuring the impact of learning with AI in Sierra Leone and beyond
items.summary:
Google DeepMind conducted a randomized controlled trial in Sierra Leone involving 1,763 junior secondary students to evaluate the impact of its AI-powered Gemini Guided Learning feature on math progress. Over eight weeks, students using Guided Learning showed significant improvements, with math scores increasing by up to 2.5 years of typical learning progress compared to a control group. The trial demonstrated high student engagement and a shift toward deeper conceptual understanding rather than simply seeking answers.

The study emphasized the role of teachers in facilitating AI-supported learning, with educators designing lessons and guiding classroom discussions. Teachers also reported professional growth through the use of Gemini, which helped them explain concepts more effectively. items.summary:
OpenAI has outlined its plan to develop artificial general intelligence (AGI) with a focus on safety, accessibility, and broad societal benefit. The company emphasizes that AGI should empower people, distribute benefits widely, and remain aligned with human values and control to ensure it serves humanity as a whole.

The plan draws parallels to the transformative impact of electricity, highlighting AI's potential to enhance daily life and expand human capabilities across various fields. OpenAI stresses the importance of public coordination and international cooperation to manage risks and guide the development of AI technologies responsibly, aiming to prevent concentration of power and promote shared prosperity.

items.originalTitle: How Endava is redesigning software delivery around AI agents
items.summary:
Endava, a global technology services company, is transforming its software delivery by integrating OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex into its workflows. This AI-driven approach, centered on AI agents, accelerates project delivery and reshapes enterprise processes across its 11,000-person workforce, fostering an AI-native culture where experimentation and AI integration are fundamental.

The company developed DavaFlow, an AI-native delivery methodology that embeds OpenAI technology throughout the software development lifecycle, from planning to deployment. Beyond engineering, AI adoption has expanded to legal, finance, and operations teams, streamlining tasks such as research, reporting, and internal tool creation. Leadership actively uses AI to enhance communication and coordination, making AI a core part of daily work rather than a separate initiative.

Endava emphasizes that successful AI adoption requires behavior change, leadership involvement, and early inclusion of non-technical teams. Looking ahead, the company envisions enterprise AI evolving into integrated systems combining models, agents, workflows, and human expertise, fundamentally changing organizational operations and establishing AI as the operating model itself.

items.originalTitle: Dreaming: Better memory for a more helpful ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched Dreaming V3, an advanced memory system for ChatGPT Plus and Pro users in the US, designed to enhance the model's ability to retain context, track user preferences, and maintain relevance across conversations. This new system builds on previous memory features by synthesizing information from multiple interactions to provide fresher and more accurate responses without relying solely on explicit memory commands.

Dreaming V3 improves upon earlier versions by automatically curating and updating memories in the background, allowing ChatGPT to better understand ongoing user needs and preferences over time. Users can review and manage their stored memories through a summary page, enabling more personalized and context-aware interactions. The update aims to make ChatGPT more helpful by remembering useful details and adapting to changes, with plans to expand availability to more users and regions in the coming weeks.

OpenAI has launched a biodefense action plan centered around its advanced AI model, GPT-Rosalind, to enhance biological threat detection and pandemic preparedness. Introduced in April 2026, GPT-Rosalind supports research in biology, drug discovery, and medicine, aiming to improve health outcomes by accelerating scientific understanding and therapeutic development. Recognizing the dual-use nature of these technologies, OpenAI is also focusing on equipping trusted developers with tools to strengthen biological security while ensuring responsible deployment through safeguards and governance.

The plan seeks to build a more resilient biological future by enabling earlier threat detection, faster countermeasure development, and more coordinated crisis response. OpenAI's initiative reflects a commitment to leveraging AI advancements to improve global health security and pandemic readiness.

items.originalTitle: Introducing new capabilities to GPT-Rosalind
items.summary:
OpenAI has released an updated version of GPT-Rosalind, a model designed specifically for life sciences research. The new update integrates GPT-5.5’s advanced coding and tool-use abilities with enhanced expertise in medicinal chemistry, genomics, and broader biological analysis, improving performance across drug discovery and experimental workflows.

The update was evaluated using LifeSciBench, a benchmark developed to assess models on comprehensive life sciences tasks including evidence handling, scientific reasoning, and experimental validation. GPT-Rosalind demonstrated significant gains in addressing complex research challenges, such as analyzing clinical trial data and supporting drug development decisions, and is now available for research preview to qualified organizations worldwide.

Wasmer used OpenAI's Codex with GPT-5.5 to develop a Node.js runtime for edge computing, reducing the development time from one year to just two weeks. This breakthrough allows developers to run JavaScript applications in a WebAssembly sandbox without relying on Docker, making Wasmer the first cloud provider to offer full Node.js support at the edge.

The Wasmer team leveraged Codex throughout the project, from initial architecture to debugging, benefiting from its advanced reasoning capabilities across multiple programming languages and low-level code. This accelerated development enabled the small company to achieve ambitious goals typically reserved for larger organizations, opening the door to more complex projects in the future.

items.title: OpenAI outlines public policy agenda focusing on AI safety, youth protection, workforce transition, and global standards to ensure AI benefits society [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: OpenAI public policy agenda
items.summary:
OpenAI has released its public policy agenda focused on ensuring that artificial general intelligence (AGI) benefits all of humanity. The agenda emphasizes AI safety, protecting youth, supporting workforce transitions, and establishing global standards to promote equitable access and responsible development of AI technologies. OpenAI aims to collaborate with governments and civil society to address risks, expand opportunities, and foster democratic participation in shaping AI's future.

The policy priorities include advancing frontier AI safety through transparency, accountability, and regulatory frameworks at both state and federal levels in the US, as well as promoting international cooperation on AI standards. OpenAI supports measures to mitigate risks related to advanced AI models, including national security concerns, while advocating for inclusive access to AI tools across diverse demographics. The agenda reflects OpenAI's commitment to adapting policies as AI evolves to ensure broad societal benefits.

items.title: OpenAI outlines a federal blueprint for U.S. governance of frontier AI focusing on safety, resilience, and national security [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: A blueprint for democratic governance of frontier AI
items.summary:
OpenAI has released a blueprint proposing a federal framework for the governance of advanced AI systems in the United States, focusing on safety, resilience, and national security. The plan emphasizes building on existing state laws and strengthening the role of the Center for AI Safety and Innovation (CAISI) as the primary federal institution overseeing frontier AI safety. It also calls for a coordinated government effort to address the broader challenges posed by rapidly advancing AI technologies.

The blueprint highlights recent state initiatives such as California's SB 53, New York's RAISE Act, and Illinois's SB 315, as well as the White House's executive order on AI innovation and security, as foundational steps. OpenAI stresses the importance of creating a durable and adaptable federal governance structure that can evolve alongside AI advancements to ensure public safety and national security.

items.title: Travelers deploys AI-powered Claim Assistant using OpenAI models nationwide to provide 24/7 customer support and scale claims processing [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Travelers deploys AI-powered claims countrywide with OpenAI
items.summary:
Travelers has launched an AI-powered Claim Assistant nationwide, utilizing OpenAI's real-time models to provide customers with 24/7 support for filing auto property damage claims. The assistant guides users through the claims process using natural conversation, answering policy questions and submitting claims autonomously. Since its initial rollout in eight states, the tool has expanded across the country, with 85–90% of customers completing their claims through the AI system.

The AI Claim Assistant helps Travelers manage high volumes of claims, especially during catastrophe events that can generate over 100,000 claims in days. By integrating OpenAI models with its claims infrastructure, Travelers ensures seamless, scalable operations without wait times, allowing claim professionals to focus on complex cases requiring human expertise.

items.originalTitle: Codex for every role, tool, and workflow
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced new role-specific Codex plugins, interactive sites, and annotations designed to enhance AI-driven workflows for various teams including analysts, marketers, designers, investors, and others. These tools integrate with popular apps and workflows to help users generate reports, create marketing assets, manage sales processes, design products, and analyze investments more efficiently without requiring coding skills.

The new plugins cover a range of functions such as data analytics, creative production, sales, product design, public equity investing, and investment banking, with plans to expand into additional areas like corporate finance and legal. Additionally, Codex now supports creating and sharing interactive websites and apps within workspaces, enabling teams to collaborate and track progress through shared URLs. This development aims to make Codex more adaptable to diverse professional roles and workflows, fostering greater productivity across different industries.

items.title: OpenAI calls for global AI Safety Institute to enhance youth protections and opportunities ahead of G7 Leaders’ Summit in June 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Advancing youth safety and opportunity through global leadership
items.summary:
OpenAI has proposed the creation of a global AI Safety Institute aimed at enhancing protections and opportunities for young people as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into education and daily life. This initiative, highlighted ahead of the G7 Leaders’ Summit in June 2026, seeks to establish international collaboration to develop consistent safety standards, share research, and provide practical guidance for youth AI use.

The proposed institute would build on existing efforts like Common Sense Media’s Youth AI Safety Institute and partnerships with educators and researchers, including projects in Estonia and the United States. OpenAI emphasizes the importance of age-appropriate safeguards, regular risk assessments, parental controls, and transparent communication about AI’s benefits and risks to ensure safe and supportive AI experiences for young users.

OpenAI plans to work with governments, civil society, academia, and industry partners to promote sustained global leadership on youth AI safety, aiming to maintain momentum beyond the G7 summit and adapt to the evolving technological landscape.

items.title: OpenAI breaks ground on 1GW data center in Michigan with community partnerships, creating over 2,500 union construction jobs and investing $10 million in local projects [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Building the infrastructure for the Intelligence Age in Michigan
items.summary:
OpenAI has begun construction on The Barn, a 1GW data center campus in Saline, Michigan, as part of its Stargate project to build AI infrastructure. The initiative aims to expand AI access, create over 2,500 union construction jobs, and invest $10 million in local community projects, including improvements to the Saline Recreation Center. The project also promises to protect local resources and prevent increased costs for local residents.

The data center will use a closed-loop cooling system to minimize water use and will not pass infrastructure costs onto local ratepayers. OpenAI is partnering with local organizations and government officials, including Governor Gretchen Whitmer, to ensure the project supports Michigan's workforce through union jobs and apprenticeship programs. Additionally, OpenAI plans to provide up to $45 million in Codex credits to eligible Michigan students to enhance AI literacy and workforce training.

This development is part of a broader effort to foster economic growth and technological leadership in Michigan, supporting local schools and services through projected tax revenues of $1 billion over the lease term. The project reflects a commitment to building AI infrastructure responsibly while investing in the communities that host it.
